clue.text: He doesn't believe guy is in shed

indicators.note: in places the man-and-is pair inside the shed word

parts.note: a hut is a shed
a guy is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sulking in a garden shed refuses to believe anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb (cast off) but is the garden hut. The definition is a whole phrase: a humanist rejects religious belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanist holds a non-religious outlook, rejecting faith in any god.

clue.text: Rotten ma renews pa's clothes

indicators.note: rotten suggests something gone bad and broken up, so the letters of ma renews are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum is grumpily replacing Dad's worn-out wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' shuffles MA plus RENEWS; 'pa's clothes' is a playful way to say garments for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments made for males, as worn by a father, are sold as this.

clue.text: It's a big block of French flats, not one with rent in arrears

indicators.note: in arrears means behind, so the rent word comes at the end

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for one from the flats word

parts.note: flats are apartments
A is one, as in a single thing
rent, the past tense of tear, gives tore

explanation.surface: A large Parisian apartment block where tenants are behind with their payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' drops A from APARTMENTS; 'in arrears' puts TORE (rent as in torn) last. 'Rent' looks like money owed but is the verb tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shop with many departments occupies a big building, often a whole block.

clue.text: Guide covers centre of Luton in a page, perhaps

indicators.note: covers means the guide word wraps round the letter taken from Luton

parts.note: a courier is a guide for tourists

indicators.note: centre of picks out the middle letter of the town name

explanation.surface: A tour guide hides the middle of Luton inside a page of a brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts T, the centre of Luton, inside COURIER. LUTON is a town north of London. 'Page' is the royal attendant, not a sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A page attended a royal court, so is one example of an attendant at court.

clue.text: Affect bloke with oboe, playing trivial work

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are messed about with, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone affects a bloke by playing the oboe to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges AFFECT, BLOKE and OBOE, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A large showy picture volume left out for guests is lightweight reading, hence trivial work.

clue.text: How one feels, caught in a downpour?

explanation.surface: Describing one's state when trapped outside in heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means feeling ill; the question mark flags the literal reading of being beneath the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means feeling poorly, as one may say of one's health; literally, someone in a downpour stands beneath the rain.

clue.text: Pretty girls showing a bit of leg in big top

indicators.note: in places the a-plus-letter pair inside the big top word

parts.note: a big top is a circus tent

indicators.note: a bit of leg is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Showgirls flash a little leg under the circus big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives L from leg; with A, it goes 'in' TENT. Talent is British slang for attractive people.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, attractive young people collectively are called this, as in eyeing up the local crowd.

clue.text: Catch girlfriend up, but runs off

indicators.note: off means the runs letter is taken away
up, in a down clue, says the girlfriend word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a girlfriend is a partner
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with their girlfriend, but she flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PARTNER to RENTRAP, and 'runs off' removes one R.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone is to catch them by trickery.

clue.text: Critic of psychoanalysis

parts.note: reads like a person who disputes Freud, but means the inner judging voice described by psychoanalysis

explanation.walkthrough: Not someone who attacks psychoanalysis, but the internal critic that Freudian theory describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's model names the part of the mind that acts as conscience and judges the self.

clue.text: Loyalty of Cuban metropolis not constant

parts.note: Fidel Castro was the famous Cuban leader

indicators.note: not signals the constant letter is dropped from the city word

parts.note: a metropolis is a city
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Questioning how loyal the Havana capital is.
explanation.walkthrough: FIDEL stands for the Cuban leader Castro; 'not constant' removes C from CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness and loyalty are synonyms.

clue.text: Fat character needs stick after short trip

indicators.note: after places the stick word behind the shortened trip
short means the trip word loses its final letter

parts.note: to trip is to fall
a staff is a stick

explanation.surface: A portly person needs a walking stick after a minor stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: FALL cut short gives FAL, then STAFF. Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's famously corpulent knight.

clue.text: Taxi from here to your gate?

definitions.text: Taxi from here to your gate?

parts.words: Taxi from here to your gate?
parts.note: taxi is the aircraft verb, not a cab: a plane taxis from the landing strip to the terminal gate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxi' suggests a cab ride home, but planes taxi from the airstrip to the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft land on this strip and then taxi along to the terminal gate.

clue.text: Ruined desert site could be close

indicators.note: ruined suggests destruction, so the letters of desert site are rearranged

explanation.surface: An abandoned spot in the desert might be nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' shuffles DESERT SITE. 'Close' is the noun, a short residential road, not the adjective near.
explanation.definitionFit: A close is a minor residential road, a kind of minor street off a main one.

clue.text: New vet entered with hay. Horses jump at it

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of vet entered and hay

explanation.surface: A newly qualified vet arrives with hay, at a show where horses leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges VET ENTERED plus HAY. This equestrian contest includes dressage, cross-country and showjumping over three days.
explanation.definitionFit: This equestrian competition includes cross-country and showjumping phases with fences.

clue.text: Preserve strength internally, right inside beam

indicators.note: internally takes the inner letters at the very centre of strength
inside places the right letter within the beam word

parts.note: to beam is to shine

explanation.surface: Keep a solid beam inside the building to preserve its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' takes the two letters at the exact centre of the eight-letter word strength, and 'inside' tucks R into the beam word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine something is to cherish and protect it, as in preserving rights in law.

clue.text: More than one getting valediction in song from Little Feat, it's said

definitions.text: More than one getting valediction in song

explanation.surface: A fan of the band Little Feat bids farewell in song.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Toot, Toot, Tootsie, Goodbye' bids farewell to a Tootsie; 'Little Feat' (the US rock band) sounds like little feet, which in baby talk are tootsies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is the sweetheart in the farewell song; in nursery talk, toes or small feet are also called this.

clue.text: Girl in car's pretentious

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the car make

parts.note: Lada is a Russian car make
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl sitting in a car is putting on airs.
explanation.walkthrough: DI goes 'in' LADA, a cheap Russian car.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected, posh-sounding behaviour is described with this mocking phrase.

clue.text: Crikey, cereal in beard

indicators.note: in places the cereal word inside the exclamation

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise, like crikey
oat is a cereal

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at finding cereal caught in a beard.
explanation.walkthrough: OAT goes 'in' GEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed tuft of hair on the chin is a style of beard.

clue.text: Discussed business: has kept old nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of has kept old are jumbled

explanation.surface: Reporting that a squirrel has kept old nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges HAS KEPT OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means chatting about work matters, as colleagues do over a drink.

clue.text: Well-known fellow has affairs (no resistance!)

indicators.note: no signals the resistance letter is removed

parts.note: amours are love affairs
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A notorious man whose love affairs meet no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: F for fellow, then AMOURS with 'no resistance' removing R.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous and well-known are synonyms.

clue.text: Support bottom half of bed

parts.note: butt is slang for the bottom

indicators.note: half of keeps only the second four letters of the bed word

parts.note: a mattress is a bed

explanation.surface: A bottom resting on half the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' needs a synonym for bed first: of its eight letters, only the back four are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting structure that props up a wall.

clue.text: Returning from Laos, outrivalled great player

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A great sportsman returns from Laos, having beaten his rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the run OSOUTRIV from 'Laos, outrivalled' and 'Returning' turns it round. A virtuoso is a great musical player, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a highly skilled musician, an outstanding performer on an instrument.

clue.text: Shrub conceals skinny dipping in river

indicators.note: dipping in puts the skinny word into the river

parts.note: the Oder is a European river
skinny means lean

explanation.surface: Bushes hide someone skinny-dipping in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is the river between Germany and Poland. 'Skinny dipping' reads as one phrase but splits into the synonym and the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen flowering bush.
